### Data Preparation

```{r setup, echo=TRUE, results='hide', warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

# Load both Insurify datasets from GitHub.

state_rates <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jmald1987/DATA606_Insurance_Premiums/refs/heads/main/auto_insurance_rates_by_state_000.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

vehicle_rates <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jmald1987/DATA606_Insurance_Premiums/refs/heads/main/auto_insurance_rates_by_vehicle_000.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Convert monthly columns from wide to long format.

state_long <- state_rates %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^20[0-9]{2}[-_][0-9]{2}$"),
    names_to = "month",
    values_to = "premium"
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    state = state_id,
    month = as.Date(
      paste0(gsub("_", "-", month), "-01")
    ),
    state_premium = as.numeric(premium)
  )

vehicle_long <- vehicle_rates %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^20[0-9]{2}[-_][0-9]{2}$"),
    names_to = "month",
    values_to = "premium"
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    vehicle = vehicle_name,
    month = as.Date(
      paste0(gsub("_", "-", month), "-01")
    ),
    vehicle_premium = as.numeric(premium)
  )

# National insurance premium benchmark.

national_rates <- state_long %>%
  filter(
    state == "US",
    state_premium > 0
  ) %>%
  select(
    month,
    national_premium = state_premium
  )

# New York and Wyoming state premiums.

selected_states <- state_long %>%
  filter(
    state %in% c("NY", "WY"),
    state_premium > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    state = recode(
      state,
      NY = "New York",
      WY = "Wyoming"
    )
  )

# Honda Civic and Honda CR-V premiums.

selected_vehicles <- vehicle_long %>%
  filter(
    vehicle %in% c(
      "Honda Civic",
      "Honda CR-V"
    ),
    vehicle_premium > 0
  )

# Combine datasets using reporting month.

analysis_data <- selected_states %>%
  inner_join(
    national_rates,
    by = "month"
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    selected_vehicles,
    by = "month"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    state_adjustment =
      state_premium / national_premium,

    estimated_premium =
      vehicle_premium * state_adjustment
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(estimated_premium),
    estimated_premium > 0
  )

# Confirm that all four combinations are present.

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(analysis_data$state) == 2,
  n_distinct(analysis_data$vehicle) == 2,
  nrow(analysis_data) > 0
)
```

### Research question

**How do estimated full-coverage automobile insurance premiums for the Honda Civic and Honda CR-V compare between New York and Wyoming, and what do these differences suggest about automobile insurance affordability?**

This project investigates the relationship between geographic location, vehicle model, and estimated automobile insurance costs.

New York is the primary location of interest, while Wyoming provides a comparison state represented in the available insurance dataset.

The study will compare estimated insurance premiums across the two states and two Honda models using monthly premium observations.

The objective is to identify differences in estimated insurance costs that may help prospective car buyers evaluate the financial implications of vehicle selection and geographic location.

### Cases

Each case represents a unique combination of state, vehicle model, and reporting month.

The four state-vehicle combinations are:

- New York — Honda Civic
- New York — Honda CR-V
- Wyoming — Honda Civic
- Wyoming — Honda CR-V

The source datasets contain monthly observations from January 2021 through October 2026.

The final number of cases depends on the number of months shared by the datasets after excluding missing or zero-valued premiums.

```{r cases, echo=TRUE}
analysis_data %>%
  summarise(
    total_cases = n(),
    reporting_months = n_distinct(month),
    states = n_distinct(state),
    vehicle_models = n_distinct(vehicle)
  )

analysis_data %>%
  count(state, vehicle, name = "observations")
```

### Data collection

The project uses secondary data published by Insurify, an automobile insurance comparison platform.

Two publicly available datasets were downloaded and stored in the project's GitHub repository:

1. Automobile insurance premiums by state.
2. Automobile insurance premiums by vehicle model.

Both datasets contain monthly premium information. The original datasets are organized in wide format, with reporting months represented as separate columns.

The data will be imported into R, converted to long format, and matched by reporting month.

The state dataset provides insurance premium information for New York, Wyoming, and the United States national benchmark.

The vehicle dataset provides premium information for the Honda Civic and Honda CR-V.

The national benchmark will be used to calculate a state adjustment factor.

The estimated state-adjusted vehicle premium is calculated as:

\[
\text{Estimated Premium}
=
\text{Vehicle Premium}
\times
\frac{\text{State Premium}}{\text{National Premium}}
\]

The calculation produces an estimated premium for each state-vehicle combination based on published aggregate insurance data.

### Type of study

**Observational study.**

The study uses previously collected insurance premium data. No variables are manipulated, and no drivers are assigned to vehicles or geographic locations.

The research compares estimated insurance premiums across states and vehicle models.

The analysis is intended to identify patterns and differences rather than establish a causal relationship between geographic location, vehicle choice, and insurance pricing.

### Data Source

**Insurify — Car Insurance Data Center**

https://insurify.com/car-insurance/report/data/

**Automobile insurance rates by state**

https://github.com/jmald1987/DATA606_Insurance_Premiums/blob/main/auto_insurance_rates_by_state_000.csv

**Automobile insurance rates by vehicle**

https://github.com/jmald1987/DATA606_Insurance_Premiums/blob/main/auto_insurance_rates_by_vehicle_000.csv

The datasets are publicly available and were not collected directly by the researcher.

### Describe your variables?

**Response variable**

Estimated automobile insurance premium, measured in U.S. dollars.

- Type: Quantitative (numerical).
- Role: Response variable.

**Explanatory variables**

**State**

- Values: New York and Wyoming.
- Type: Qualitative (categorical).
- Role: Explanatory variable.

**Vehicle model**

- Values: Honda Civic and Honda CR-V.
- Type: Qualitative (categorical).
- Role: Explanatory variable.

**Reporting month**

- Type: Temporal.
- Role: Used to match datasets and examine premium trends over time.

**Additional quantitative variables**

- State insurance premium.
- National insurance premium.
- Vehicle-model insurance premium.
- State adjustment factor.

The main analysis will examine how the estimated response variable differs across the two categorical explanatory variables.

### Relevant summary statistics

The following statistics will be calculated for each state and vehicle combination:

- Number of observations.
- Mean estimated premium.
- Median estimated premium.
- Standard deviation.
- Minimum estimated premium.
- Maximum estimated premium.

Visualizations will compare the distribution, average cost, and monthly trends of estimated premiums.

```{r summaries, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# Overall case count and reporting periods.

analysis_data %>%
  summarise(
    total_cases = n(),
    reporting_months = n_distinct(month)
  )

# Summary statistics by state and vehicle model.

summary_table <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(state, vehicle) %>%
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    mean_premium = mean(estimated_premium),
    median_premium = median(estimated_premium),
    sd_premium = sd(estimated_premium),
    min_premium = min(estimated_premium),
    max_premium = max(estimated_premium),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        mean_premium,
        median_premium,
        sd_premium,
        min_premium,
        max_premium
      ),
      ~ round(.x, 2)
    )
  )

print(summary_table)

# Visualization 1:
# Distribution of estimated premiums by state.

ggplot(
  analysis_data,
  aes(
    x = state,
    y = estimated_premium,
    fill = vehicle
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Automobile Insurance Premiums",
    subtitle = "Honda Civic and Honda CR-V: New York vs. Wyoming",
    x = "State",
    y = "Estimated Premium (USD)",
    fill = "Vehicle Model"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Visualization 2:
# Average estimated premium by state and vehicle.

average_premiums <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(state, vehicle) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_premium = mean(estimated_premium),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  average_premiums,
  aes(
    x = vehicle,
    y = mean_premium,
    fill = state
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    position = "dodge"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Estimated Insurance Premium",
    subtitle = "New York and Wyoming",
    x = "Vehicle Model",
    y = "Average Estimated Premium (USD)",
    fill = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Visualization 3:
# Estimated insurance premium trends over time.

ggplot(
  analysis_data,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = estimated_premium,
    color = state
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ vehicle) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Insurance Premium Trends",
    subtitle = "Honda Civic and Honda CR-V",
    x = "Reporting Month",
    y = "Estimated Premium (USD)",
    color = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Compare average premiums between the two states.

state_comparison <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(vehicle, state) %>%
  summarise(
    average_premium = mean(estimated_premium),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = state,
    values_from = average_premium
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    difference = `New York` - Wyoming
  )

print(state_comparison)
```
